oewn-02452235-v.learner: to give someone the right to have or do something.
examples: I am almost the nearest relation he has in the world, and am entitled to know all his dearest concerns.
But you are not entitled to know mine

oewn-01031533-v.learner: to give something a title (a name).
examples: She entitled her first book 'Summer Rain'.

oewn-02403605-v.learner: to give someone a title, making them a member of the nobility (the group of people with high rank, such as lords).
examples: The king entitled the brave soldier, and from then on he was called Sir John.

oewn-01455372-a.learner: having or making a sound that is very big or very strong.
examples: The loud thunder woke the baby.

oewn-02402358-s.learner: too bright or showy, in a way that shows poor taste.
examples: He wore a loud shirt covered in orange and pink flowers.

connotation.why: judges bright colours or showy style as lacking taste, unlike 'bright' or 'colourful'

oewn-01461579-a.learner: (in music) showing that a piece or part of a piece should be played loudly.
examples: The last part of the song is marked loud, so the band plays it with full force.

oewn-11438574-n.learner: something no one can know or predict that makes things turn out well.
examples: I only hope they may have half my good luck.
If she heard me, it was by good luck, for I am sure she did not listen.

oewn-11438252-n.learner: something no one can know or predict that makes an event turn out one way and not another.
examples: Whether the coin lands heads or tails is only a matter of luck.

oewn-14496806-n.learner: your general situation in life, including everything that happens to you.
examples: Through all the hard years, he never once complained about his luck in life.
But, luckily, he came back again in ten minutes' time, and then we all set out.
she is luckily too poor to be an object of prey to anybody.

oewn-05481998-n.learner: a bundle of very thin threads (fibres) that runs to the organs and other parts of the body.
examples: The doctor said the fall had damaged a nerve in his arm.
Halfway up the cliff she lost her nerve and could not go on.

oewn-04845441-n.learner: rude, pushy boldness that shows no respect for others.
examples: He broke my window and then had the nerve to ask me for money.

connotation.why: judges boldness as rude, unlike 'boldness' or 'courage'

oewn-00907805-v.learner: to accept someone's excuse for something they did.
examples: never had she before been so much disposed to pardon his interference in the views of his friend.

oewn-00907352-v.learner: to officially free someone from the punishment for a crime.
examples: The governor pardoned the prisoner, and he walked free the next day.
Anger and jealousy are passions that can be hard to control.

oewn-07503928-n.learner: a feeling of strong sexual desire.
examples: a couple who were only brought together because their passions were stronger than their virtue

oewn-05821331-n.learner: anything that you love warmly or are deeply devoted to.
examples: Music has always been her passion.

oewn-04635549-n.learner: the quality of being a person with very strong feelings.
examples: He was a man of great passion, quick to love and quick to anger.

oewn-14062661-n.learner: something that you want very, very much.
examples: His passion was a house by the sea, and he saved for twenty years to buy one.

oewn-09204454-n.learner: a reason for believing or doing something that is not sensible but that you cannot resist.
examples: Driven by a strange passion he could not explain, he checked the locks again and again all night.

oewn-03905025-n.learner: a way made especially for one particular use.
examples: The path just admitted three.
before she could strike into another path, she was overtaken by Wickham.

oewn-00416689-n.learner: a way of behaving that someone follows.
examples: He chose the path of honesty, even when it cost him his job.

oewn-09410115-n.learner: the line or route along which something travels or moves.
examples: The storm destroyed every house in its path.

oewn-08633886-n.learner: a fixed, usual way of travelling to or getting into a place.
examples: The guide showed us the usual path from the village to the lake.

oewn-01917434-a.learner: having the training and meeting the standards and requirements needed for a job, position or task.
examples: I am not qualified to form one.
she would find me in every respect ill qualified for the situation.

oewn-01919581-a.learner: limited in some way; not complete or total.
examples: The plan won only qualified approval from the committee.

oewn-01965069-s.learner: having the right official papers and being on record as allowed to do a certain job or use a certain skill.
examples: He is now a qualified pilot, with his licence on record.
Their offer is qualified on your passing the final exam.

oewn-01545039-s.learner: having its meaning narrowed by another word, as 'man' is in 'a tall man'.
examples: In 'a tall man', 'man' is a qualified noun, because 'tall' narrows its meaning.

oewn-07235246-n.learner: a short telling of something that happened, especially something in a person's life.
examples: They could describe an entertainment with accuracy, relate an anecdote with humour, and laugh at their acquaintance with spirit.
Lady Catherine was generally speaking--stating the mistakes of the three others, or relating some anecdote of herself.
